newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire recalls governor who ordered Tutsis to leave.
newsitem.headline: Zaire recalls governor who ordered Tutsis to leave.

text.p: Zaire's central government has recalled the regional administrator who ordered about 200,000 ethnic Tutsis to leave eastern Zaire where they are embroiled in fighting with the army, a government spokseman said on Monday.
But spokesman Boguo Makeli said the army would pursue its campaign against Tutsi rebels that has pushed tension in the region bordering Rwanda and Burundi to boiling point.
Boguo said, however, he could not confirm reports that South Kivu Deputy Governor Lwasi Ngabo Lwabanji had been sacked for giving ethnic Tutsis or Banyamulenges a week to leave, expiring on Tuesday.
"I am aware that he has been recalled to Kinshasa," he told Reuters.
Lwabanji, who has accused the Banyamulenge of destabilising the region, was still in South Kivu on Monday.

Aid workers say they fear all-out war in the sub-region because of the quit order. The Rwanda army, which is dominated by Tutsis, has exchanged fire with Zairean troops and the Burundi army, also predominnatly Tutsi, risks being drawn in.

Banyamulenge Tutsis settled in Zaire from Rwanda about 200 years ago. Clashes between them and indigenous peoples have degenerated into virtual civil war since more than a million rival Rwanda Hutus fled violence into the same region in 1994.
